result:
Done. Both gates are green (`bun run typecheck` clean, `bun test` 5 pass / 0 fail), and `bunx guren check` reports 0 failures.

I made the server the single source of truth for the sign-up form. In `routes/auth.ts` the `register.store` route now carries the existing `RegisterSchema` as its `body` contract (`guest.post('/register', { name: 'register.store', body: RegisterSchema }, [RegisterController, 'store'])`), which is codegen-only in this framework — route contracts validate params/query/output at request time but not bodies, so `RegisterController.store()` still does the `validateBody(RegisterSchema)` call and the 422/redirect behaviour, validation rules, route name and path are all untouched. Regenerating with `bun run codegen` published `ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']` in `.guren/api-client.gen.ts`, and `resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx` now derives its form type from that (`type RegisterFormData = ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']`), posts via `route('register.store')` from `.guren/routes.gen.ts`, and reads messages from `form.errors` — so the hand-written `RegisterFormData`, the hand-typed `errors` prop and the hard-coded `/register` path are all gone (`.guren/pages.gen.ts` regenerated accordingly, dropping the now-absent `auth/Register` props entry). I verified the guards by applying the misspellings repo-wide under `resources/js/`: renaming `passwordConfirmation` fails typecheck at all four sites (initial values, `form.data`, `setData`, `form.errors`), and `register.stor` fails at both the type lookup and the `route()` call. I also added `tests/RegisterController.test.ts` covering the page render and the 422 error keys (`passwordConfirmation`, `name`, `email`), priming CSRF via `withCsrf()` since sign-up is a protected POST; it stays database-free like the existing suite, so the happy-path account creation is left to the external acceptance checks.
